qa.overall_assessment: Critical bug in exit code handling: Node.js reports exitCode=null for signal kills (SIGKILL, SIGTERM), but code treats exitCode===null as clean exit. OOM-killed sessions (SIGKILL) will NOT be respawned, directly violating AC1. Additionally, peak merge in watcher still writes archived sessions back to session_dirs.txt, which ExecStartPost will restore on daemon restart.

root_cause_verification.rationale: The architectural change (daemon-level respawn instead of watcher auto-restore) is correct in design. The watcher auto-restore trigger is removed. However, the exit code handling has a critical bug (exitCode===null for signal kills is treated as clean exit), which means the daemon respawn path is broken for the most important use case (OOM kills). Additionally, peak merge still writes archived sessions back to session_dirs.txt, creating a path for session resurrection on daemon restart.

code_quality_findings.issue: exitCode===null is treated as clean exit, but Node.js reports exitCode=null for ALL signal kills (SIGKILL from OOM, SIGTERM from external). This means OOM-killed sessions will NOT be respawned. Verified with actual Node.js test: SIGKILL produces code=null, signal='SIGKILL'.
code_quality_findings.recommendation: Change line 686 to: const isCleanExit = exitCode === 0 || (exitCode === null && signal === null); This way, signal-based exits (SIGKILL, SIGTERM) are NOT treated as clean exits and will enter the respawn path (unless stoppingByDaemon is set).

code_quality_findings.issue: Peak merge still writes archived sessions back to session_dirs.txt. Scenario: user archives 3 sessions -> count drops -> peak merge writes them back -> daemon restarts -> ExecStartPost reads session_dirs.txt -> archived sessions are restored. This defeats the purpose of removing the watcher auto-restore trigger.
code_quality_findings.recommendation: Either (1) remove peak merge entirely from update_snapshot_with_peak_protection since the daemon now handles crash recovery, or (2) only write peak-merged data to JSON snapshots (for audit) but NOT to session_dirs.txt. The session_dirs.txt should only reflect the current running state.

code_quality_findings.issue: stoppingByDaemon flag is set in stopSession() but never checked by onChildExited for those sessions, because stopSession deletes the session from pidToTrackedSession (line 654) before the exit event fires. The flag works as defense-in-depth if the code is refactored, but currently has no effect.
code_quality_findings.recommendation: Either move pidToTrackedSession.delete(pid) from stopSession into onChildExited (so the flag is actually checked), or document that the delete-before-exit pattern is the primary protection. Moving the delete to onChildExited would also fix the missing notifySessionEnd call for stopped sessions.

code_quality_findings.issue: stopSession does not call apiMachineRef.notifySessionEnd(), and the session is deleted from the map before onChildExited fires (which also calls notifySessionEnd). Result: server is never notified when a session is stopped via RPC. This is a pre-existing issue, not introduced by this change.
code_quality_findings.recommendation: Add apiMachineRef?.notifySessionEnd(session.happySessionId) in stopSession before deleting from the map.

all_findings.issue: Peak merge in update_snapshot_with_peak_protection still writes archived sessions back to session_dirs.txt. On daemon restart, ExecStartPost will restore these archived sessions, defeating the event-driven architecture.
all_findings.recommendation: Remove peak merge from session_dirs.txt writes, or disable peak merge entirely now that daemon handles crash recovery.

all_findings.issue: stoppingByDaemon flag is dead code because stopSession deletes session from map before exit event fires. Server not notified of session stop (notifySessionEnd never called for stopped sessions).
all_findings.recommendation: Move pidToTrackedSession.delete(pid) from stopSession to onChildExited so the flag is actually checked and notifySessionEnd is called.

refined_context.recommended_approach: 1. Fix the exit code check at run.ts:686 to: const isCleanExit = exitCode === 0 || (exitCode === null && signal === null). This ensures signal-based exits (SIGKILL from OOM, external SIGTERM) enter the respawn path. The stoppingByDaemon check at line 689 already handles daemon-initiated SIGTERM. 2. Consider removing or limiting peak merge in update_snapshot_with_peak_protection to prevent session_dirs.txt from containing archived sessions that would be restored on daemon restart.
refined_context.additional_context: Verified with Node.js runtime test: child.kill('SIGKILL') produces exit event with code=null, signal='SIGKILL'. Same for SIGTERM: code=null, signal='SIGTERM'. The BA spec mentions exit codes 137/143 which are bash $? conventions, not Node.js ChildProcess event values. Node.js uses null exitCode + signal string for signal-based kills.
